correctness_confidence.basis: The entire paper is backed by exact rational arithmetic certificates verifying LP primals, duals, and dimension-independent Horn inequalities. The proofs mapping these to stability constants are logically sound.

novelty.basis: The exact fractions for N=6 to 12, the (A_N, B) cost law for N up to 14, and the 22-form exact formula for kappa_6 are original to this work, upgrading previous numerical guesses to explicit theorems.

reproducibility.basis: The paper provides comprehensive, zero-dependency Python scripts using standard library fractions to explicitly replay and verify all JSON certificates exactly, alongside the generation scripts.

rigor.basis: The mathematical architecture rigorously translates the Klyachko-Knutson-Tao bounds into finite, exact certificates. Fallbacks to rationalized duals ensure no floating-point taint. Lemma 4.1 guarantees dimensional stability.

significance.basis: Solves a concrete open question in matrix analysis and algebraic combinatorics (Hilbert-Schmidt norm of commutators) through an innovative mixture of hive models and automated exact theorem proving.

potential_errors: No fatal errors detected. The gap between generic Horn recursion and explicitly generated templates is closed correctly via the stability lemma.
strengths: Uses an elegant dimension-independent template structure to generalize d=2N bounds to all d >= 2N.
Flawless separation of floating-point generation and exact rational verification, removing any numerical instability doubts.
Complete reproducibility package provided in the supplement, allowing immediate verification of all certificates.
strong_novelty_candidates: Exact rational values for gamma_{N,d} for N=6 through 12.
The specific 22-form formula for the six-level trace-zero cost kappa_6, along with its chamber decomposition.
Proof of the (A_N, B) cost law up to N=14.
summary: This manuscript presents a computer-assisted exact computation of the balanced-inertia stability constants for inverse self-commutators for N=3 to 12, proving their exact rational values in all dimensions d >= 2N. It leverages Klyachko's formulation of Horn's inequalities and Knutson-Tao's hive model, reducing the infinite-dimensional family of optimization problems to a finite set of exact rational certificates (hive primals and windowed Horn duals). The author provides exact rational Python verifiers for these certificates, which confirm the (A_N, B) cost law up to N=14 and rigorously extract the 22-form exact formula for kappa_6. The methodology is mathematically rigorous, the code separates floating-point discovery from exact fractional verification, and the dimension-independent stability argument (Lemma 4.1) is robust. The paper represents a definitive solution to the specific numerical conjectures posed in prior literature.
weaknesses: Highly specialized topic; the impact is largely restricted to researchers working on matrix commutators, Horn inequalities, and Schubert calculus.
The theorems are almost entirely computer-verified with few conceptual geometric proofs of why the minimizers switch at N=7.
